# Your Name Is on the Label—Do You Own It? — finished platform kit

## 1. LONG VIDEO
“Your name is stitched into the label. Now show me the record.” Open on the Sollers advertisement, then split the visible name into seven evidence lanes: human identity, company, federal mark, license, domain, platform account, archive. Walk through consent under 15 U.S.C. §1052(c), assignment under §1060, and the limits of what those records establish. Close: the label is the public signal; the control map is the institutional evidence.

## 2. SHORT 01
“Your name on the garment is not a complete ownership search.” In 45 seconds, show a label branching into mark, company, domain, likeness, archive, and approval rights. On screen: SAME NAME ≠ SAME RECORD. End: identify the asset before claiming the right.

## 3. SHORT 02
“Consent to register a living person’s name is not the same as permanent control of every use.” Show consent, registration, assignment, license, and approval as separate cards. Final card: U.S. issue spotting only—take the actual records to counsel.

## 4. CAROUSEL
Frame 1: YOUR NAME IS ON THE LABEL. Frame 2: WHO OWNS THE MARK? Frame 3: WHO OWNS THE COMPANY? Frame 4: WHO ADMINISTERS THE DOMAIN? Frame 5: WHO CAN LICENSE THE NAME? Frame 6: WHO APPROVES THE PORTRAIT? Frame 7: WHO CONTROLS THE ARCHIVE? Frame 8: WHAT CHANGES BY TERRITORY? Frame 9: ATTACH THE RECORD. Frame 10: THEN ASK COUNSEL.

## 5. NEWSLETTER
Subject: Your name is visible. Is your control? The edition opens with the difference between public recognition and record evidence, explains the two federal trademark provisions without overclaiming, gives the eight-field control inventory, and ends with the four categories this educational audit cannot decide.

## 6. LINKEDIN
A name can be identity, reputation, mark, company asset, domain, handle, license subject, and archive authority at once. Those layers may align—or split. Before a founder says “I own my name,” build a record-by-record map: asset, owner, authorized user, territory, term, approval, recovery, unresolved question.

## Claim ledger
- **VERIFIED:** Section 2(c) of the Lanham Act bars registration of a mark that consists of or comprises the name, portrait, or signature identifying a particular living individual without written consent. (S48)
- **VERIFIED:** A federally registered mark and the human identity it references are distinct interests; recorded assignments may transfer a registered mark subject to statutory conditions. (S48, S49)
- **INFERENCE:** The label display alone does not establish who owns a mark, company, domain, likeness right, or contractual approval power. (S48, S49, S32)

## Publication discipline
This is U.S.-bounded educational issue spotting, not legal advice. Do not add unlicensed imagery. Preserve captions, alt text, creator and institution credits, canonical URLs, evidence labels, jurisdiction limits, and counsel-review gates.
